review_candidates.title: Chief Executive Officer - Lyrasis
review_candidates.description: Organization Overview: Lyrasis Lyrasis is a mission-driven nonprofit that provides technology, content, and shared services to libraries, archives, museums, and other knowledge communities. Through its scale, expertise, and collaborative approach, Lyrasis helps these institutions expand access to information, preserve and share cultural heritage, strengthen their technology infrastructure, and increase their impact. Lyrasis is a fully remote organization with a staff of over 110 employees, more than 1,000 member institutions and thousands of other organizations that use its products, services, and programs. Lyrasis operates as both a membership organization and a service provider. Many of its products and services are available to members and non-members alike, allowing organizations to partner with Lyrasis based on their individual needs. Members receive preferential pricing, access to specialized services and programs, voting rights in the Board of Directors elections, and are invited to participate in discussions that help shape Lyrasis’ priorities. This model allows Lyrasis to combine the collective strength of a membership organization with the reach and capabilities of a large-scale technology and services enterprise. Supported by organization-wide functions spanning Membership, Human Resources, Fiscal Services, IT, and Operations, Lyrasis delivers its products and services through three primary departments: Content & Scholarly Communication Initiatives : Helps institutions access content more affordably and advance new models for scholarly communication. Lyrasis uses its collective scale to negotiate e-content licensing and pricing, supports open-access initiatives and open research infrastructure, and works with partners to develop more equitable and sustainable approaches to accessing and sharing scholarly content. Community Supported Technologies & Hosting Services : Provides a sustainable home and infrastructure for important open-source technologies used by libraries, archives, and museums. Lyrasis supports technologies including ArchivesSpace, DSpace, Fedora, and VIVO, while providing hosting and related services that help institutions manage, preserve, and provide access to digital collections and research. Ebooks & Community Engagement : Expands how libraries provide and create digital content for their communities. Through The Palace Project, The Indie Author Project, and BiblioBoard, Lyrasis provides ebook access and marketplace solutions, helps libraries discover and elevate local authors, and offers tools for collecting and sharing locally created digital content. Lyrasis fosters a workplace culture that embodies its values of communication, respect, collaboration, and service. The organization is committed to building a future that is inclusive, equitable, accessible, and sustainable. Formed in 2009 through the merger of three regional library networks with legacies dating back to 1936, Lyrasis has continued to expand its reach and capabilities, through its merger with DuraSpace and the acquisition of BiblioLabs. Lyrasis is deeply grateful to outgoing CEO John Wilkin, who will retire after four years of transformative leadership. John stepped into the role following a period of significant expansion and helped lead Lyrasis through tremendous growth, with gross revenue increasing from $88 million in FY22 to $134 million in FY26. Even more defining has been the significant cultural transformation under his leadership. John has played a pivotal role in strengthening Lyrasis internally, leading organizational restructuring that realigned departments, teams, and reporting relationships to create a more cohesive and collaborative organization. These changes have fostered greater staff voice, shared decision-making, and empowerment across the organization. The next CEO will inherit a deeply committed team, a strong organizational structure and culture, and strengthened trust and credibility with Lyrasis’ members and communities. Guided by its values of community, belonging, and resilience, Lyrasis is well-positioned for its next chapter of growth. With a strong foundation, Lyrasis has the opportunity to deepen its value to members and customers, embrace emerging technologies, and expand its impact across the knowledge and cultural heritage sector. Position Summary: Chief Executive Officer Lyrasis seeks a strategic Chief Executive Officer to shape the organization’s next era of growth and impact. Reporting to the Board of Directors, the CEO will oversee a $134 million organization with more than 100 employees, including six direct reports across the executive and senior leadership teams. The next CEO will lead the development of a clear, forward-looking vision and strategy for Lyrasis - bringing greater clarity to who the organization is, where it is going, and the unique role it can play across the library, archive, museum, and knowledge communities. They will connect opportunities across Lyrasis’ diverse portfolio, strengthen its external identity and visibility, and position the organization to expand its relevance and impact. This leader will bring an entrepreneurial lens to the future, anticipating shifts in technology and the evolving needs of the communities Lyrasis serves and identifying where the organization can innovate, partner, invest, and grow. At the same time, they will be deliberate in how they lead - taking the time to deeply understand Lyrasis’ people, products, services, and stakeholders and building upon what is working before charting what comes next. The ideal candidate will bring deep expertise in the knowledge and cultural heritage sector, with a strong understanding of the institutions, stakeholders, and evolving landscape Lyrasis serves. They will be energized by the opportunity to lead a complex, evolving organization and bring the strategic perspective to see across Lyrasis’ many areas of work, and the leadership to engage staff, members, customers, partners, and board members in creating a shared vision for the future. Key Responsibilities Strategic Vision & Leadership: Partner with the Board and leadership team to develop and execute a compelling vision and long-term strategy that aligns Lyrasis’ diverse portfolio, strengthens its identity, and advances its mission. Board Partnership & Governance : Build a strong, transparent relationship with the Board of Directors, providing strategic guidance, financial and organizational reporting, and the information needed for effective governance. Engage the Board in setting priorities, evaluating opportunities, and advancing Lyrasis’ long-term vision. Organizational Leadership & Culture : Lead and empower a fully remote, multidisciplinary team. Preserve Lyrasis’ collaborative, mission-driven culture while strengthening cross-departmental alignment, shared accountability, staff engagement, and professional development. Membership & Customer Engagement : Deepen relationships with members and customers, understand their evolving needs, and ensure Lyrasis delivers meaningful value through its products, services, and programs. Strengthen engagement, satisfaction, and long-term relationships across the communities it serves. Positioning & External Leadership : Serve as Lyrasis’ chief ambassador, articulating its value and raising its visibility across the knowledge and cultural heritage ecosystem. Build relationships with institutional leaders, industry organizations, technology partners, and other stakeholders to strengthen Lyrasis’ reputation and influence. Innovation & Growth : Anticipate emerging trends in technology, scholarly communication, and the evolving needs of libraries, archives, and museums. Identify and evaluate opportunities for new products, services, strategic investments, and mission-aligned growth. Financial Stewardship & Sustainability : Provide strategic oversight of Lyrasis’ financial performance, operating budgets, investments, and long-term sustainability. Balance entrepreneurial investments with disciplined financial management, thoughtful resource allocation, and measurable organizational impact. Enterprise Integration & Operational Excellence : Provide oversight across Lyrasis’ departments, strengthening coordination, identifying opportunities for shared resources and capabilities, and ensuring effective execution. Establish organizational priorities and performance measures while preserving the expertise and distinct value of individual programs. Strategic Partnerships & Collaboration : Cultivate partnerships, alliances, and collaborative initiatives that advance Lyrasis’ mission and extend its capabilities. Evaluate opportunities for joint ventures, acquisitions, and other strategic relationships based on their long-term value to the organization and the communities it serves. Technology & Product Strategy : Guide the strategic direction of Lyrasis’ technology platforms, open-source initiatives, content services, and digital products. Work with senior leaders to assess investments, product sustainability, emerging technologies, and opportunities to strengthen the organization’s competitive position and community impact. Leadership Competencies MISSION ALIGNMENT & SECTOR CREDIBILITY The next CEO will bring a genuine connection to Lyrasis’ mission and a commitment to equitable information sharing, open access, and connectivity across knowledge communities. They will bring leadership experience and credibility across libraries, archives, museums, higher education, research institutions, or related nonprofit spaces, ideally with experience leading a complex organization with a broad portfolio of products and services. INTENTIONAL & EMPOWERING LEADERSHIP Lyrasis seeks a thoughtful, deliberate leader who will listen and learn before acting. The CEO will value staff expertise, invite diverse perspectives into decision-making, and give teams the trust, resources, and space to experiment with new ideas. They will preserve and advance Lyrasis’ strong culture of collaboration, inclusion, and belonging while continuing to strengthen connection across a fully remote organization. STRATEGIC VISION & FOCUS The next CEO will bring clarity to where Lyrasis is going and where it can have the greatest impact. They will collaboratively develop a cohesive strategy that connects Lyrasis’ diverse programs and services, sharpens organizational priorities, and helps the organization make thoughtful choices about what to pursue - and what not to pursue. This leader will translate a broad range of possibilities into a focused vision that staff, Board members, and external communities can understand and rally around. INNOVATION & FINANCIAL STEWARDSHIP With significant financial resources, Lyrasis has an opportunity to invest creatively in its mission. The CEO will bring strong financial acumen and experience managing significant organizational resources, pairing sound stewardship with an entrepreneurial mindset. They will identify community needs, invest in promising ideas and new products, and ensure resources are deployed thoughtfully to create sustainable mission impact. EXTERNAL LEADERSHIP & COMMUNITY CONNECTION The CEO will be a visible and credible ambassador with the communication and relationship-building skills to engage a broad range of stakeholders. They will strengthen Lyrasis’ presence and reputation nationally and globally, cultivate partnerships, and clearly communicate the organization’s value and vision. Most importantly, they will stay connected to emerging needs and opportunities, ensuring that Lyrasis’ future is shaped in partnership with the communities it exists to serve. Location, Compensation and Benefits This is a fully remote position, and the CEO may be based anywhere in the United States. As the external leader of a national and global organization, the CEO will travel regularly to build relationships with members, customers, partners, and other stakeholders, attend industry convenings, and connect in person with Lyrasis’ distributed team. The anticipated salary range is $350,000 - 380,000, commensurate with experience. Lyrasis offers a comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental, and vision coverage; generous retirement contributions and paid time off; as well as, other benefits designed to support employee well-being and professional growth. Interest in the Role? To express your interest and explore this opportunity, please submit your resume and cover letter via the Maneva website. All inquiries and discussions will be handled with the utmost confidentiality. This position is available immediately, and applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until the role is filled. Lyrasis is committed to fostering a diverse, equitable, inclusive, and accessible workplace and strongly encourages applications from candidates of all backgrounds, experiences, and identities, including those from historically underrepresented communities. En mai 2026, plus de 1,46 million de personnes étaient déplacées à l'intérieur du pays, souvent dans des sites surpeuplés et précaires. Appuyer le suivi sur le terrain des activités des partenaires de mise en œuvre : avancement par rapport aux plans de travail, collecte et vérification des données et des rapports, et compte rendu au/à la chargé(e) de protection ;
